title: Is it Poetry Saturday on Substack?
subtitle: Inspired by my friend Awais Aftab, selected poems
body_html:
I woke up to the following post from , entitled “I Don’t Know What Will Save Me: And Other Poems.” Poetry is the least commercial of art forms. Fewer people read my posts published on a Saturday, too! Maybe it will fly entirely under the radar? This post serves to stand with my poet colleagues, like Awais. It also serves as notice that I’m going to a poetry reading later with my friend Chris Akin, and that is just a coincidence.

Instead of learning anything or diving into any data, I’ll offer three poems. I’m an award-losing poet, recall. I have two published books of poetry: The Hellthread and Why We Skeet. These photos are also taken by me— I shot quite a few over the years. Most of the photos used in this newsletter were taken by me if they weren’t collages or AI-absurdity.

We Were Too Young to Know How Sick We Were 

The river
From the banks
And from 
The endless
Sickly
Storm
That was born of
The torrid affair
You had
With the North Dakota sky

Don’t leave me a
Pauper
But a bigger beggar
For more
No less for none have seen

A heroic turn
From the proud
Merciless boys
I knew when i was your age and they were not mine

Jennifer knew me then
She knew Enough
To stay away

Hey nightmare notes
The symphonic disklavier
That plays along
As if a piano could 
Fiddle
With the violin
The 

Devil himself played 
Down to Georgia

The ocean is so vast
You will drown i promise
The tides said to me
Quiet or loud
The sand bar will be washed

Clean by being washed away

How many feet will the Ocean
Rise till the stilts

Become the lampposts
Of a shittier movie
Than the one we wrote
About heroes
And villains
And our inability to make
The kind of nonsense

Palatable
To those with
Tender feelings
Uncertain auspices
And the heavy light
Of inauspicious stars
Breathed
Out and in and never again

Merry Lordships
Turn dreadful
As we measure
The inches between
Insolvent hopes and 
Terrific dreams
On the

Verge of the
Wreck
Of something great

I lived once
And a summer
Home might be out of reach now

Satan, I cast thee
Out of my heart

And the lord forgave that trespass 
As we were trespassers, all

Oceans of oceans of land mines still
Archipelago dances
All the way

To the notional ground
I was abraded
Heavy
Unburden yourself to me
Because I kill
Like you live
Without mercy me
When there is none to go around 

A Tirzepatide appetite for 
Justice
And an infinite hunger
For having some 
Way

Of explaining to those i love
Why i lived and why they died
The way i did
That looses
A good 
Chance
To 
Tie 
My
Sins
In 
A 
Bow.

A dark night full of jokes
That the king, queen, ace, and rook
Felt like was 54 cards
And two that could be let go.
Jack, or joker?
Don’t make me choose.

But you won’t
Time
Sense
And semaglutide will print paucity
To my platter, like none
My heart would know

The tuner 
Measures to the cent
Of the off-pitch 
Note 
I sang at my 
Eulogy 

Time is not Enough
For you
And too much for me

That is the first one from The Hellthread, written on a plane in 2022. The next is from another plane ride, the same year, and is more humorous in bent.

Objectives and Key Results for Assholes 

Wire frames of what we intend
And my life needs a product management 
Hire 
That is, strong, or so management said.
But the interviews are not going well
And finding individuals of quality
To unfuck this mess is proving
To be ambitious.

My key performance indicators 
For leaving less of a mess behind 
Are discussed in the shower
Which, sadly, is as quarterly 
As our reviews. 
And once the quorum
Between me, myself
And I is reached—
I talk to myself 
And echos flutter with haas effect shit
That any self-respecting engineer 
Would have filtered out.

Objective: to cause less resentment in everyone
As measured by
A 20% reduction quarter over quarter
In complaints about my character on the internet
And 30 text messages in Q2 that express
Positive regard.

Luckily, me and myself love measurement-based
Living.
I, on the other hand, has been a real
HR nightmare 
And we might have to let him go.
But he’s likely to sue for hostile work environment.
So consider this poem
Documentation
Of a pattern of behavior
That we will use to fight this 
Self-hating guy
When he tries to take the whole fucking
Enterprise Down.

And the third is, before this moment, unpublished. So, here we go.

Hallelujah, Lost

Terrible temerity
Tacitly left
For dead and gone
Blamed the other
And othered the fault
Forgot the forgone
An obligation to the others
Obey, Await, servile

Taken from me
And from all of us
By circumstances relentless
Forces beyond those we understood
River, rock, riven
Through shore, ravenous
Early to Ravenna
And late to the latent

Enrich yourself while you still
Plan to do whatever gets you there
Nothing less, and not more
Than everything
We need to need to fulfill our endless
Gaping emptiness

Table the motion
Unseat the king
Better kill him
Best to kill me too

Wailing waters
Floods brought us low
Indemnity from our sins
Convert our indulgences
Into a more fungible form
It's the wettest we could get
In terms, I'm told, of water

Share
